title: Broccoli e Salsiccia
subtitle: Short pasta with Italian sausage and broccoli
excerpt: Crumbled Italian pork sausage cooked with broccoli and garlic, tossed through short pasta with a little pasta water to bring it together. Fast, filling, and full of flavour.
sourceNotes: Classic southern Italian pairing of sausage and broccoli, widespread in Puglia and Calabria.

content.text: Sausage and broccoli is a weeknight staple across southern Italy. The sausage fat does the work of a sauce. Keep a mug of pasta water back and add it a splash at a time so everything coats evenly.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the broccoli florets and cook for 3 minutes. Scoop them out and set aside. Keep the water on the heat.
Drop the pasta into the same water. Cook according to the packet until al dente. Reserve a large mug of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over a medium heat. Add the sausage meat and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Push the sausage to the side. Add the garlic and chilli flakes to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant but not brown.
Add the blanched broccoli. Press some of it down to break it apart. Stir everything together and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the drained pasta to the pan. Pour in a splash of pasta water. Toss well over the heat for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy.
Season with black pepper. Serve straight away with grated parmesan if you like.

items.cause: Not enough pasta water was added when tossing.
items.fix: Add another splash of the reserved pasta water and toss again over a low heat until loose.

items.symptom: The sausage is dry and crumbly.
items.cause: The heat was too high when browning it.
items.fix: Add a small splash of pasta water to the pan and stir it in. The starch will bind things together.

items.cause: It was blanched too long or cooked again in the pan for too long.
items.fix: Keep the pan toss short and the heat moderate. Aim for tender florets that still hold their shape.
